A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AAPO research. All 18 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: v2 reports original AAPO evaluations on mathematical reasoning benchmarks, clipping ablations, and training analyses in Tables 1–2 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds reference-model and group-size experiments, computational measurements, pass@k evaluations, and MMLU and LiveCodeBench results.

M1.justification: The AAPO objective, clipped policy/reference reward difference, frozen reference model, and training procedure remain unchanged in Equations (4)–(6) and Algorithm 1. Advantage momentum is renamed advantage margin. Reference-model replacement is investigated as an ablation, without replacing the proposed method.

E1.justification: v3 adds evaluation beyond mathematical reasoning: MMLU across 57 subject domains for both Qwen-based AAPO models and LiveCodeBench for AAPO-1.5B. The original training datasets and five mathematical benchmarks are retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 and the original-paper comparison retain the same comparator membership, including GRPO, GPG, and the named Qwen reasoning baselines. New evaluations compare against existing base models or GRPO; no new external comparison algorithm is introduced.

E3.justification: v3 adds pass@k evaluation using 64 responses, group sizes 2/6/10, reference updates every 20/100 steps, and resource profiling. Appendix C.2 reverses the reported 1.5B/7B training-prompt assignments. D.2/Table 6 identify the main 7B setting as G=6, conflicting with C.2's retained G=8. These reporting changes do not establish reruns.

E4.justification: The clipping ablation and existing training analyses are retained, with the latter moved to D.4. v3 adds fixed-versus-updated reference comparisons, group-size sensitivity tests, measured zero-advantage trajectories, and pass@k analyses probing behavior beyond single-response accuracy.

E5.justification: Neither version documents seeds, independent repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The reported training-loss variances are unchanged. Sampling 64 responses for pass@k adds an evaluation protocol rather than repeated-run uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 and the original-paper comparison retain their scores. New results include reference-update averages of 55.4/51.0 versus 56.7/52.4 with frozen references, LiveCodeBench scores of 25.78 versus 27.01, and 7B MMLU scores of 25.96 versus 39.65 for base versus AAPO models. New pass@k results frequently place AAPO-1.5B below its base model.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–2 and most derivations are retained. However, Appendix B's reorganized assumptions omit v2's explicit strictly positive standard-deviation condition, sigma_min > 0, while the stability bound still divides by sigma_min. This is a limited but substantive omission in the formal assumptions.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: diagnose group-relative advantage inefficiencies, augment advantages using reference-model rewards, and demonstrate superior mathematical benchmark performance. The terminology change and additional supporting experiments do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly acknowledges remaining zero advantages and increased training time. It explains why updating the reference weakens the margin, interprets out-of-domain transfer, and qualifies reasoning improvements through the larger-k shortcomings of AAPO-1.5B. These substantially expand the account of applicability, mechanisms, and tradeoffs.

D1.justification: v3 adds an AAPO code-access URL, explicit training and benchmark sample counts, the model.generate implementation disclosure, resource measurements, and the 7B context limit of 4,096 tokens. Appendix C.2 revises prompt assignments, while most reward, hardware, batch-size, and accumulation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 removes the general LLM background paragraph and associated citations, while adding references for MMLU, LiveCodeBench, vLLM, and Yue et al.'s discussion of RLVR reasoning capacity. The main positioning relative to GRPO, GPG, and other RL methods remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 renames momentum to margin throughout, updates author information, trims related work, adds theoretical transitions, and moves training analyses to Appendix D.4. It adds Limitations and AI-use disclosure sections, but preserves most existing prose and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. v3 replaces the conceptual Figure 1 with empirical trajectories, adds multiple result displays and a training-sample column, reformats Algorithm 1, and relocates or resizes retained clipping, training, and loss plots.

improvement.justification: v3 improves empirical support and transparency through mechanism ablations, measured computational costs, larger-k shortcomings, and explicit limitations. These benefits are partly offset by unexplained training-prompt reversals, conflicting 7B group-size reporting, and omission of the positive-variance assumption. The added evidence makes the paper more informative, but these reproducibility and formal-documentation problems limit the overall gain.
